A class member without a modifier is public. A reader cannot tell whether that was decided or forgotten, and a helper that was meant to be private becomes part of the class's API. This rule makes you write the modifier on every property, method, accessor, constructor and parameter property.

Members with a `#private` name are never reported.

A missing modifier is not fixed, because only you know which one is right. The report offers all three as suggestions. With `"no-public"`, `--fix` removes the `public` keyword.

## Examples

Reported:

{/* bad {"count": 3} */}
```ts
class Account {
  balance = 0;

  constructor(readonly owner: string) {}
}
```

Not reported:

{/* good */}
```ts
class Account {
  private balance = 0;
  #history: number[] = [];

  public constructor(public readonly owner: string) {}
}
```

## Options

| Option | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `accessibility` | `"explicit"` | `"explicit"` requires a modifier. `"no-public"` reports `public`, since it is the default anyway. `"off"` checks nothing. |
| `overrides` | `{}` | A different level for one kind of member: `accessors`, `constructors`, `methods`, `properties`, `parameterProperties`. |
| `ignoredMethodNames` | `[]` | Names of methods and accessors that are never reported. |

With `"no-public"`:

{/* bad {"options": [{"accessibility": "no-public"}]} */}
```ts
class Account {
  public balance = 0;
}
```

{/* good {"options": [{"accessibility": "no-public"}]} */}
```ts
class Account {
  balance = 0;
  private pin = "";
}
```

A parameter needs a modifier to become a property. So `"no-public"` allows `public` there when it stands alone, and reports it next to `readonly`:

{/* good {"options": [{"accessibility": "no-public"}]} */}
```ts
class Account {
  constructor(public owner: string) {}
}
```

{/* bad {"options": [{"accessibility": "no-public"}]} */}
```ts
class Account {
  constructor(public readonly owner: string) {}
}
```

With `overrides`, constructors can go without a modifier while everything else needs one:

{/* good {"options": [{"overrides": {"constructors": "no-public"}}]} */}
```ts
class Account {
  private balance = 0;

  constructor() {}
}
```
